**Low confidence, and honestly it might be lower than that once you look closer.**

Good catch spotting the shared source — that's the whole ballgame here. Three blog posts citing #4521 isn't three confirmations, it's one report wearing three hats. The blogs add no independent evidence; they're just distribution, not verification.

Two things I'd want before calling this "solid":

1. **What #4521 actually says.** Is it a confirmed repro with a maintainer response, or an open report someone filed and nobody's triaged? Those are very different levels of evidence, and I can't tell which from "three blogs link to it" — I don't have a way to pull up the issue myself right now, so I haven't seen the content, just the fact that it's the common root.
2. **Whether anyone's reproduced it independently** — a second, unrelated report of the same symptom (different repo, different user, different context) would actually add confidence. Three restatements of the same one don't.

So right now: this is a single unverified report until someone reads #4521 itself and checks whether it's substantiated (repro steps, maintainer ack, fix landed, etc.) — not three-source-confirmed like it looked at first glance.
